rv.q: But when you’ve got material of this quality, it needs less extra food than you think; a few drops of blood and it can grow on an audience all by itself.
Paramount Theatre has reinvented this popular musical and taken it to a whole new level, thanks to an army of creative theatre artists.
This production is set proudly in near-future New York, where creepy hyperbole and slapstick reign.

Along the way, Ashman and Menken’s brilliant collaboration shines in the capable hands of music director Kory Danielson who conducts the Paramount Band and choreography by Michael George and Mariah Morris. LaGamba’s lofty and poignant rendition of “Somewhere That’s Green” and the superb duet with Ball “Suddenly, Seymour” are particular highlights.
Fleming and her cast deliver, peppering Paramount's production of writer/lyricist Howard Ashman and composer Alan Menken's sweet, comically macabre musical with amusing stage business.
This is a well-directed effort from Landree Fleming.
Overall, Paramount Theatre's production of Little Shop of Horrors is a must-see for musical theatre fans.
The folks at Paramount are pretty special at building a team to bring wonderful shows on a consistent basis.

cn.t: Critics praise Paramount Theatre's "Little Shop of Horrors" as a visually stunning, vocally delightful production that delivers big laughs and entertainment, with director Landree Fleming and a talented cast bringing fresh energy to the beloved musical.
